## Source
.design/m5/47-trust-model.md — Q1 follow-on + decomposition PR 8 (conditional).

## Surface (conditional on Q1)
- IF Q1 lands on B (mini-DSL): `polaris-trust/src/parse.rs` — `nom`- or `chumsky`-based parser for expressions like `if observation.category == "spam" then 0.9 * decay(60d) else 0.5`. Evaluator integrates into `weight()` as the `custom_factor`.
- IF Q1 lands on C (JSON Logic / Rego): integrate `jsonlogic` crate or `regorus` for Rego evaluation. Similar `custom_factor` integration.
- IF Q1 stays on A: this PR is closed without changes. v2 baseline is sufficient.

## Rust-quality notes (only if PR proceeds)
- **The DSL parser is the highest-risk component of this entire epic.** A buggy parser silently produces wrong weights → silently boosts bad labels. Per rust-quality §7: 100% line coverage required. Property tests fuzz the parser with `proptest` + `cargo-fuzz` for at minimum 1M iterations.
- **DSL evaluation is sandboxed**: no I/O, no time-of-day except `now()` (passed in), bounded recursion depth, bounded numeric operations (no division by user-supplied zero crashing the worker). Per rust-quality §10 (cancel-safety in async contexts).
- **The DSL is OPT-IN** — operators must explicitly enable it in config (`[trust] enable_dsl = true`). Default off.
- Boost-attack protection (Q6-C) is mandatory if this PR ships: the save endpoint runs a backfill simulation across the last N observations and rejects the change if aggregate weight increases by >2x.

## External references
- nom parser combinators: https://docs.rs/nom/latest/nom/
- chumsky: https://docs.rs/chumsky/latest/chumsky/
- cargo-fuzz: https://github.com/rust-fuzz/cargo-fuzz
- jsonlogic Rust impl: https://docs.rs/jsonlogic/latest/jsonlogic/

## Acceptance (conditional)
- [ ] If Q1 = B or C, this PR ships the DSL/expression parser with property tests + fuzzing.
- [ ] If Q1 = A, this issue closes without code; v2 ships without custom expressions.
